### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.snippets

### Question

Is it possible to run a Lua function while expanding a snippet to achieve dynamic behaviour? E.g., I want to do something like this:

```lua
  {
    prefix = "fun",
    desc = "Regular function",
    body = {
      function()
        return "function! " .. autoload_name() .. "($2) abort"
      end,
      "  $3",
      "endfunction",
      "",
    },
  },
```

where `autoload_name` will give the current files "autoload prefix". E.g. it could output `vimtex#foo#bar#$1` if I'm inside the file `autoload/vimtex/foo/bar.vim`.

Notice, if I were to inline the above function, i.e.

```lua
  {
    prefix = "fun",
    desc = "Regular function",
    body = {
      "function! " .. autoload_name() .. "($2) abort"
      "  $3",
      "endfunction",
      "",
    },
  },
```

then the snippet expansion will not change when I change the file.

comment_data.bodyHTML:
Yes, it is possible because entries in config.snippets can be function loaders. So this requires creating a local function (not possible to put that in a separate file, I am afraid) and use it inside require('mini.snippets').setup() as part of config.snippets.

Here is an example:

local vim_autoload_snippet = function(context)
  local buf_name = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(context.buf_id)
  local autoload_suffix = buf_name:match('autoload[\\/](.+)%.vim$')
  if autoload_suffix == nil then return {} end

  local autoload_name = autoload_suffix:gsub('[\\/]', '#')

  return {
    {
      prefix = 'fun',
      desc = 'Regular function',
      body = {
        'function! ' .. autoload_name .. '#$1($2) abort',
        -- I'd suggest using here `$0` tabstop directly
        '  $0',
        'endfunction',
        '',
      },
    },
  }
end

local minisnippets = require('mini.snippets')
minisnippets.setup({
  snippets = {
    -- Other snippet loaders go here
    vim_autoload_snippet,
  },
})

> So, does this mean that if I create my own snippets e.g. in `~/.config/nvim/snippets/vim.lua`, then I can let some of the snippets be functions instead of tables, where the functions need to return a snippet table?

In theory - yes. In practice - `read_file()` doesn't support callable values and I am not sure why... I'll take a closer look and maybe update it. Plus maybe add a note about "dynamic snippets" to [general advice about management](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/228a8c34fae1d778e895ad06e4158f65e85828bc/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L350-L351).

reply_data.body:
That sounds good. I just migrated from my 10+ year old Ultisnips setup, and I think dynamic snippets are the one thing I will miss if it is not available. The variable interpolation is sufficient in 90% of the cases, but some times I think the ability to generate the body at call time is very useful.

I realize it is possible with the custom loader, but I think it would be much better with regard to usabliity if it was possible to either allow the `body` to be a function that returns a string or list of strings, or let the entire snippet be a function that returns a table.

reply_data.body:
> ... or let the entire snippet be a function that returns a table.

Yes, this is already possible, as stated before. Even from custom Lua file, which returns an array of snippets: each either snippet table, function, or array of those.

It is just that built-in `gen)loader.from_file('path/to/file')` does not currently support that (it checks for every array element to be a snippet table). I don't remember why it is the case and will take a closer look.

reply_data.body:
`read_file()` should now work with functions as returned item. So something like this is now possible:

- Create a file '~/.config/nvim/snippets/vim-autoload.lua' with the following content:

    ```lua
    local autoload_snippet = function(context)
      local buf_id = context.buf_id
      -- ...
    end

    return { autoload_snippet }
    ```
- Use the following setup:

    ```lua
    local snippets, config_path = require('mini.snippets'), vim.fn.stdpath('config')
    snippets.setup({
      snippets = {
        snippets.gen_loader.from_file(config_path .. '/snippets/vim-autoload.lua'),
        -- The rest of the snippets
      },
    })
    ```
